title: Declarative JSON Call Profiles, Soft Validation, and User-Facing Error Hints
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a pragmatic, developer-friendly JSON schema format for function/tool calling that supports:
- declarative parameter profiles (required/optional/soft-required),
- multi-version compatibility (compatibility layers for older SDKs),
- soft validation modes (warnings vs. hard errors),
- standardized, actionable error messages and error codes for both SDKs and the Console.

Background & Motivation:
Existing runtime validations are strict by default and produce short, opaque messages that surface as developer friction and support tickets. Teams integrating Redwood function-calls (tooling, external APIs, private deployments) have asked for: better migration paths when parameter shapes evolve, lower-friction dev onboarding, and error messages that contain a concrete remediation hint and a stable error code to map telemetry/alerts.

Goals & Acceptance Criteria:
1) Define a compact, declarative manifest format for call parameter profiles that can be embedded in model metadata or served from the model registry. Manifest must express: param name, type, default, stability (stable | experimental | deprecated), enforcement level (disabled | warn | enforce), and a short remediation_hint string.
2) Implement soft validation that emits telemetry+warning in SDK logs when enforcement=warn but returns 200 to allow compatibility testing.
3) Define a canonical error envelope with: code (e.g., CALL_PARAM_MISSING), path (JSONPath-ish string), human_message, remediation_hint, and link to docs. All fields are strings.
4) Provide an SDK mapping table for legacy SDKs: map new enforcement levels to SDK behaviors (legacy: always enforce -> map to enforce; modern: support warn mode).
5) Add Console UI support to surface top-10 param warnings per model version and links to failing request samples for quick debugging.

Design decisions & trade-offs considered:
- Compact manifest vs full JSON Schema: full JSON Schema is expressive but too verbose for most model authors. We adopt a lean manifest that covers 90% of real-world needs and can reference a full JSON Schema via a 'schema_url' when needed.
- Soft validation increases false positives in telemetry if not guarded. We'll gate telemetry emission with a sampling rate and a per-model opt-out flag.
- Error envelope must be stable; we choose short, namespaced error codes (CALL_*) to avoid collisions with other subsystems.

Manifest example (compact, intentionally human-readable):

{
  "version": "v2",
  "params": [
    { "name": "user_id", "type": "string", "stability": "stable", "enforcement": "enforce", "remediation_hint": "Provide a non-empty user_id; use the lookup endpoint if unknown." },
    { "name": "max_results", "type": "integer", "stability": "experimental", "enforcement": "warn", "default": "10", "remediation_hint": "Pass an integer between 1 and 100. Using default=10 may affect recall." },
    { "name": "metadata", "type": "object", "stability": "stable", "enforcement": "disabled", "remediation_hint": "Optional free-form map; not used for ranking yet." }
  ]
}

Note: the runtime will accept the above as a string-encoded manifest; when 'schema_url' is present the runtime will fetch and validate against full JSON Schema on first use (with caching).

Error envelope example (human-readable):
{
  "code": "CALL_PARAM_TYPE_MISMATCH",
  "path": "$.params.max_results",
  "human_message": "The 'max_results' parameter must be an integer.",
  "remediation_hint": "Convert the value to an integer or remove the field to use the default.",
  "doc_url": "https://confluence.redwood.ai/call-schema-v2#errors"
}

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) Schema format & runtime parser (ENG): define proto manifest schema and implement server-side parser + cache (2 weeks).
2) Soft validation mode (ENG): implement enforcement levels and telemetry hooks (2 weeks).
3) SDK opt-in/opt-out mappings (SDKs): map enforcement to SDK return behaviors and log formats (1 week).
4) Console telemetry surfaces (PM/Frontend): surface warnings, sampling controls, and links to request replay (2 weeks).
5) Docs & migration guide (DX/Docs): publish manifest authoring guide and suggested linting rules (1 week).

Rollout strategy:
- Alpha: model teams opt-in by adding 'manifest_url' to their model metadata. Soft validation defaults to warn with 10% telemetry sample.
- Beta: increase sampling, add default linter rules in SDKs and enable Console surfacing.
- GA: enforcement=warn becomes default for experimental fields; enforcement=enforce reserved for stable params.

Telemetry & Metrics:
We will emit metrics with tags: model_version, enforcement_level, code, and sample_rate. Top-level KPIs: number of warn events per model_version, reduction in param-related support tickets, and time-to-fix for developer-facing errors.

Backward compatibility & compatibility layers:
- Legacy SDKs that lack 'warn' plumbing will receive a header 'X-Redwood-Call-Enforcement: warn' and the gateway will translate enforcement=warn to the legacy behavior (enforce) with a notice in response headers.
- When a param is removed, authors should set stability=deprecated for at least one minor release before removal; runtime will emit deprecation warnings tied to the manifest and provide sample requests that used the deprecated field.

Open questions / Risks:
- How large should the manifest schema be (v2 vs heavier v3)? We'll iterate based on early adopter feedback.
- Legal/security review for manifest URLs in Private deployments (we may need signed manifests for air-gapped installs).
